items.title: CO2 Transport and Storage Availability Webinar
items.summary: Free virtual IEAGHG webinar on 24 November 2026 (13:00–14:00) presenting a study by TNO with SINTEF and SCCS on designing CO2 transport and storage networks for high availability and limited downtime for emitters. The study estimates realistic operational availability rates for pipeline transport and for storage in saline aquifers and depleted fields. Speakers include Ragnhild Skagestad (SINTEF), Filip Neele and Wouter Janssen (TNO) and Navraj Singh Ghaleigh (University of Edinburgh).
items.why_it_matters: Availability and downtime figures for pipelines and storage sites are direct inputs for redundancy, buffer storage and reliability constraints in CCS network-optimisation models.

items.title: Registrations open for the Innovation Fund 2026 Info Days
items.summary: CINEA has opened registration for four online Info Days on the Innovation Fund 2026 calls and auctions. The joint session on the Net-Zero Technologies call (€3.3 billion) and the new Maritime call (€200 million) takes place on 15 December 2026; other sessions on 9–10 December cover the hydrogen and heat auctions and the SME call.
items.why_it_matters: The Net-Zero Technologies call is the main EU grant route that Nordic-Baltic capture, transport and storage projects have used, so its timeline shapes the project pipeline that network models must assume.

items.title: A small labour case may have major consequences for Norwegian energy policy
items.summary: gigaCCS highlights an article by Mona Mølnvik published in Altinget.no on how a small labour case may affect Norwegian energy policy. The gigaCCS page could not be opened for further detail.
items.why_it_matters: Commentary from the gigaCCS centre on Norwegian energy-policy risk is relevant context for the regulatory stability assumed in Norwegian CCS value-chain planning.

items.title: Carbon Capture, Utilization and Storage (GRS) 2027: Science, Systems, and Society for Scaling Carbon Management
items.summary: Gordon Research Seminar on carbon capture, utilization and storage for early-career researchers, held 29–30 May 2027 at Les Diablerets, Switzerland. Abstracts to be considered for oral presentations are due 21 February 2027 and applications close 1 May 2027.
items.why_it_matters: A systems-and-society focused CCUS seminar is a venue for early-career researchers to present CCS supply-chain and network-optimisation work.

items.title: Commission invites public to shape new carbon storage certification for buildings
items.summary: The Commission has opened public feedback until 10 December 2026 on a draft certification methodology under the CRCF Regulation for carbon storage in buildings using bio-based construction materials such as timber. It is the first proposed methodology for carbon storage in products, following methodologies already adopted for permanent carbon removals and carbon farming. The Commission is also assessing applications from nine certification schemes seeking recognition under the regulation.
items.why_it_matters: Completes the CRCF methodology set and coincides with the recognition of certification schemes, which will also certify permanent removals such as BECCS whose credit revenue underpins Nordic capture-and-storage chains.
